data.body: Patients across Great Britain will continue to have access to the medical devices and in vitro diagnostic devices (IVDs) they rely on, from insulin pumps and replacement joints to diagnostic tests and surgical equipment, after the government has today, 21 October 2026, confirmed it will continue to accept CE marked medical devices on a long-term basis. The decision follows a public consultation , which ran from 16 February 2026 to 10 April 2026, that received more than 1,000 responses from patients, healthcare organisations, industry and others. The decision means the UK will not require an additional approval route for devices already approved for the EU market, avoiding duplication for manufacturers and helping to maintain stable supply and patient access to medical technologies. More than 90% of medical devices registered for use in Great Britain currently carry a CE mark, meaning they have been assessed and approved for the European market, and this approval has been recognised to provide access to the Great British market. Continuing to recognise these devices will help maintain safe, uninterrupted access to the treatments and technologies that patients and the NHS rely on. This sits alongside the UKCA marking route, which continues to operate as the domestic approval pathway for devices placed on the market in Great Britain. These arrangements sit alongside strengthened post-market surveillance and reporting requirements already in place. The MHRA will continue to oversee all devices on the UK market, monitor safety through mechanisms including the Yellow Card scheme, and work closely with international partners to share safety information enabling the MHRA to take action to protect patients where needed. In parallel, the UKCA route remains the current domestic approval route for medical devices placed on the market in Great Britain. This is being modernised through the pre-market statutory instrument, which will update the requirements devices must meet to be UKCA marked. Alongside this, we will continue to seek enabling powers through primary legislation to develop a future licencing approach for medical devices, intended to support a more modern and adaptable framework that is better able to respond to advancing medical technologies, including software and AI medical devices, reflecting recommendations from the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare. Our approach will secure supply of medical devices for UK patients while also supporting safe, rapid access to innovation so that patients can benefit from the best new technologies. By providing a clear and predictable regulatory framework. The approach supports the development and availability of new health technologies for patients, in line with the ambitions of the Government’s Life Sciences Sector Plan and 10 Year Health Plan. Continued recognition of CE-marked devices also reflects the wider ambition of the MHRA’s 2030 Strategy to expand reliance and recognition routes with trusted regulators, reducing regulatory burden, strengthen supply resilience and supporting timely patient access. Lawrence Tallon, Chief Executive of the MHRA, said: “This decision gives patients, the NHS and industry the long-term certainty they need on access to medical devices. data.body: Commitments made in the strategy will enable the regulator to keep pace with rapid advances in science, technology and personalised healthcare, to benefit patients, and position the UK as a leading place to develop, launch and use new medicines and technologies safely and effectively. The strategy defines the MHRA’s mission to contribute to ‘health and prosperity for all, through scientific excellence’ and reaffirms its central purpose to protect patients, improve public health and enable faster access to innovation. Minister for Health Innovation, James Frith said: We want patients to benefit faster from the latest medicines and technologies, while maintaining the highest standards of safety. This strategy will help the MHRA keep pace with the latest innovations in AI, data and medicine, while strengthening its ability to crack down on illegal medicines to keep the public safe. This will put patients at the heart of regulation, whoever they are and wherever they live — with greater diversity in clinical studies and a Women’s Health Plan to secure better outcomes for women. MHRA Chief Executive, Lawrence Tallon said: We are in the midst of a period of extraordinary scientific and technological discovery, which is helping to reshape how diseases can be prevented, diagnosed and treated. AI is transforming both regulated products and how organisations are run. Cell and gene therapies are offering the possibility of long-lasting or curative treatments. Precision and personalised medicines are transforming the accuracy and effectiveness of treatments. Advanced diagnostics are driving earlier intervention and better outcomes for patients. These ground-breaking developments challenge traditional regulatory models and require innovative approaches to evidence generation, clinical research design, manufacturing oversight and safety and surveillance. data.body: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has today, 26 November 2026, authorised obicetrapib and ezetimibe (Evlarco) to treat adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidaemia who have not reached their LDL-cholesterol goals despite treatment with ezetimibe and the maximum tolerated dose of a statin, or with ezetimibe alone where statins cannot be used. It may also replace obicetrapib and ezetimibe taken as separate tablets. The medicine combines two cholesterol-lowering medicines in a single tablet and is authorised for use alongside a cholesterol-lowering diet. It contains two active substances that lower cholesterol through complementary mechanisms. Obicetrapib reduces the transfer of cholesterol between lipoproteins, increasing the removal of LDL cholesterol from the bloodstream, while ezetimibe reduces the absorption of cholesterol from food in the intestine. Julian Beach, MHRA Interim Executive Director of Operations, said: High cholesterol is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease, which remains one of the leading causes of illness and death in the UK. Today’s authorisation provides an additional treatment option for patients whose cholesterol levels remain inadequately controlled despite existing therapies. As with all medicines, we have carefully assessed the benefits and risks of obicetrapib and ezetimibe. We will continue to monitor its safety closely through our robust surveillance systems. The authorisation was supported by evidence from a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial involving 407 adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, or multiple cardiovascular risk factors. Treatment with the medicine resulted in a reduction in LDL cholesterol compared with placebo. The most commonly reported side effects with this medicine are high blood pressure, dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, increased blood creatine phosphokinase, an enzyme that can indicate muscle injury, fatigue and increased blood glucose. As with all medicines, patients and healthcare professionals are encouraged to report suspected side effects through the MHRA Yellow Card scheme . Notes to editors: The approval was granted on 26 November 2026 to A. Menarini International Licensing S.A. More information can be found in the Summary of Product Characteristics and Patient Information Leaflets which will be published on the MHRA Products website within 7 days of approval. The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is responsible for regulating all medicines and medical devices in the UK by ensuring they work and are acceptably safe. All our work is underpinned by robust and fact-based judgements to ensure that the benefits justify any risks. The MHRA is an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care. data.body: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is introducing a series of new measures to strengthen how key risks associated with antidepressant medicines are communicated to patients, carers and healthcare professionals. The changes follow an extensive review initiated by the Commission on Human Medicines (CHM), in response to concerns raised by both patients and families about how information on two key areas is communicated in patient information leaflets. These are suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and sexual dysfunction that continues after treatment is stopped. Throughout the review we engaged directly with patients and families and considered the latest available evidence and expert clinical advice. Dr Alison Cave, MHRA Chief Safety Officer, said: “Patients need clear and accessible information about the benefits and risks of medicines so they can make informed decisions. “We are incredibly grateful for the valuable contributions of patients, families, clinicians and experts to this review. “These measures will help ensure patients, carers and healthcare professionals can have more informed conversations about the benefits and risks associated with antidepressant medicines, and better support people throughout their treatment.” “Antidepressants are effective medicines for the treatment of depression and other conditions. When used appropriately and under clinical supervision, for the vast majority of individuals, the benefits outweigh the risks. The aim is not to discourage use, but to improve the prominence and clarity of the existing warnings. “It’s imperative that patients do not stop taking these medicines without first speaking to their healthcare professional.” As a result of this review, patient information leaflets for antidepressants will be updated, including a new boxed warning signposting to information on suicidal thoughts and behaviours, making information easier to find. The expectation is that a new patient card will be included in or on the medicine box to reinforce key safety messaging and help patients and carers understand how and when to get further support. Patient information leaflets for certain antidepressants will be updated to include the term ‘Post SSRI Sexual Dysfunction’ (PSSD), to explain the risk of symptoms continuing after stopping treatment. This update aims to better reflect patient experiences and existing safety information. Finally, a supporting safety (ancillary) leaflet is being developed by the MHRA with the wider healthcare system, which will be given to patients at their first appointment discussing antidepressants. It will describe the key risks and benefits to support informed decision making about their treatment. This safety leaflet will also be given to patients who are already receiving antidepressants. This will be available in 2027. Chris Bird, programme manager for patient safety at NICE, said: “This review will ensure patients and healthcare professionals have the most up to date information to help them make crucial decisions on treatment and support. “We are grateful to have collaborated with the MHRA on the review, with NICE colleagues joining its expert working group. “As with all new safety advice issued from the MHRA, we will consider the implications of this advice on published NICE guidance and review our recommendations if required.” We will continue to work with partners across the healthcare system to support more consistent communication of risks…

data.body: Obicetrapib blocks the transfer of cholesteryl esters from HDL (‘good’ cholesterol) to other lipoproteins, helping to lower LDL (‘bad’) cholesterol. It is licenced to be taken on its own, or in combination with a patient’s existing cholesterol lowering therapies, and is only available on prescription, as a film-coated tablet to be taken once daily by mouth. Julian Beach, MHRA Executive Director, Operations, said: Primary hypercholesterolaemia and mixed dyslipidaemia cause high levels of blood cholesterol. We are pleased to be able to authorise a new treatment option to help people with these conditions lower their cholesterol. As with all products, we will keep the safety of obicetrapib under close review. The benefit of obicetrapib was demonstrated in two 52-week, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies involving adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia and/or mixed dyslipidaemia. In the two studies, obicetrapib reduced LDL-C by 36% and 33% respectively, compared with placebo. The maximum effect of obicetrapib in reducing LDL-C was seen as early as week four and was maintained throughout the one-year treatment period in both studies. The most common side effects with obicetrapib (which may affect up to 1 in 10 people) are dizziness; headache; high blood pressure (hypertension); abdominal pain; diarrhoea; increased blood levels of glucose; and increased blood levels of creatine phosphokinase (an enzyme released into the blood when muscle is damaged). Anyone who suspects they are having a side effect from this medicine are encouraged to talk to their doctor, pharmacist or nurse and report it directly to the Yellow Card scheme . Meanwhile, a fresh copy remains online, with recent updates linked to a user that ALPA repeatedly asked GitHub to ban. From: TF , for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.
data.title: Pirate Site Movix’s Source Code Survives Four Rounds of GitHub Takedowns

data.summary: DISH asks a New York federal court for a $21.15 million default judgment and a broad injunction against the alleged operators of pirate IPTV service DMTN. The two men, who are believed to reside in North Africa, are aware of the lawsuit but did not appear in U.S. court. Meanwhile, the service's website remains online, selling annual subscriptions for €70. From: TF , for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.
data.title: DISH Wants $21m From Pirate IPTV Operators Who Ignored Its Lawsuit

data.summary: The alleged operator of defunct pirate streaming site Movie2K could walk out of a German court a free man, and still a bitcoin billionaire. The presiding judge in Leipzig has proposed dropping the criminal case if he hands over another 40,000 bitcoin, worth roughly $2.6 billion (€2.4 billion) at today’s rate. In April, the court still proposed a suspended prison sentence in exchange for a confession. From: TF , for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.
data.title: Alleged Operator of Pirate Site Movie2K Could Walk Free as Bitcoin Billionaire

data.summary: Reddit's latest transparency report shows that it removed nearly 259,000 pieces of content in response to copyright takedown notices during the first half of 2026, 19% more than in the previous six months. At the same time, the number of users and communities banned for repeat infringement dropped sharply, with subreddit bans down 79% to 118. Reddit doesn't explain why. data.title: Reddit’s Copyright Removals Rise as Repeat Infringer Bans Drop

data.summary: A rivalry between two Miami sellers of $120 dog breed photo books has been escalated to a Florida federal court. The lawsuit accuses a rival publisher of hiring an account-ban vendor, who allegedly weaponized Meta's copyright system by filing takedown notices in the target's own name. The takedown vendor later offered to withdraw the strikes and share his client’s details if the bookseller deactivated its pages for 30 hours, so he could get paid. data.summary: After taking down Switch emulators and hacking tools on GitHub for years, Nintendo is now going after modchip firmware. The gaming company sent a DMCA notice targeting firmware for modchips such as Picofly, SX Core and HWFLY, after which GitHub disabled 144 repositories. To back its claim, Nintendo cites the criminal case against alleged Team-Xecuter members, which led to a guilty plea from one of its three defendants. data.title: Nintendo Targets Picofly Switch Modchip Firmware in GitHub DMCA Takedown

data.summary: A New York federal judge has awarded thirteen major publishers $19.5 million in damages in their lawsuit against pirate library WeLib. The default judgment also orders registries, registrars and hosting providers, including Cloudflare and Njalla, to take the site's domains offline. Whether the publishers will ever see any money is doubtful, as WeLib's operators have yet to be identified. From: TF , for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.
data.title: Pirate Library WeLib Hit With $19.5m Default Judgment and Domain Takedown Order

data.summary: Spain's court-ordered piracy blocking regime blocked the official customer support forum of Internet provider Movistar on Saturday night. A blocking notice referenced a ruling that LaLiga obtained together with the company that runs the Movistar Plus+ streaming service. On Sunday, the forum moved from Cloudflare to Amazon CloudFront, without any word from Movistar on why. From: TF , for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.
data.title: Movistar Blocks Its Own Support Forum Under LaLiga Anti-Piracy Order

data.summary: In May, a Paris court ordered DNS resolvers to block six domains that streamed pirated tennis matches. After a series of quiet, unannounced expansions, the list has since grown to 118. This includes two domain names that now belong to TorrentFreak. Notably, no domain names have been taken off the list, not even one that was seized by the U.S. Government months ago. From: TF , for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.
data.title: Inside a French Piracy Blocklist: Expired Domains, a Seized Site, and Hong Kong Servers
